mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning: Team A's possession FOR (recent vs. all-prior) crossed with Team B's shots AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior). Both dimensions must shift in the same direction (possession down for A, shots-allowed up for B) to activate the mechanism. Neither dimension alone constitutes the full condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shot production rises relative to its possession-adjusted baseline when Team B's recent defensive permissiveness (shots allowed) is elevated above its season mean, even as Team A's own possession is suppressed — suggesting a non-linear interaction between possession share and opponent defensive openness on shot volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume (FOR) is jointly conditioned by its own possession share and the opponent's (Team B's) defensive shot-allowance rate. When Team A operates below its long-run possession average AND faces an opponent whose shots-allowed rate is elevated in recent matches relative to its season baseline, Team A's shot production diverges from what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams (Team A possession FOR vs. Team B shots AGAINST), each compared across two time windows. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or same-competition split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team B's shots FOR (recent vs. all-prior uplift) AND Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior uplift). The mechanism activates when both observables show concurrent recent elevation — an asymmetric cross-team joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent shot volume is elevated above its season mean AND Team A's recent shots-on-target conceded is elevated above its season mean, Team B's shots-on-target FOR rises disproportionately relative to either team's standalone baseline — indicating a multiplicative rather than additive relationship between the two observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target conversion efficiency (shots_on_target FOR relative to shots FOR) is asymmetrically related to Team A's shots-on-target concession rate. When Team B's recent shot volume has risen sharply above its season baseline while Team A's shots-on-target conceded has also risen recently, the joint signal on on-target quality diverges from what each team's individual baseline implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a joint cross-team condition on two distinct observables (Team B shots FOR and Team A shots_on_target AGAINST), each evaluated across two time windows. Not reducible to a single observable mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on Team B's fouls FOR (recent vs. all-prior: 15.4 vs. 12.6) AND Team A's fouls AGAINST (all-prior: 11.2, below competition mean of 12.8). The mechanism tests whether the asymmetry between one team's elevated foul-committing rate and the opponent's below-average foul-drawing rate predicts yellow card volume differently than either team's card baseline alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the committing team's recent foul rate is elevated above its season mean AND the receiving team's foul-drawing rate is below competition average, yellow card volume (and second-half card accumulation) rises above what either team's standalone card baseline would predict — reflecting a non-linear foul-rate-to-card conversion under asymmetric foul pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate (FOR) has risen sharply in recent matches above its season baseline, while Team A's fouls-against (conceded) rate is below the competition average. The joint relationship between Team B's elevated recent foul production and Team A's below-average foul-drawing rate creates a cross-observable condition on yellow card accumulation that neither team's card baseline alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls FOR for one team, fouls AGAINST for the other) across two different teams, then linking to a third observable (yellow_cards / cards_2h). This is a three-observable cross-team joint relationship, not a single-observable mirror or band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on: (a) Team A's corner_kicks FOR first-half vs. second-half split (2.48 vs. 2.14) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half split (2.36 vs. 3.03); (b) Team B's corner_kicks FOR first-half vs. second-half split (2.48 vs. 2.41) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half split (2.63 vs. 2.51). The mechanism tests whether the within-match temporal distribution of corners — specifically whether a team generates more corners in the second half than the first — interacts with the cross-team corner differential to predict total match corner volume beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's corner production is back-loaded (second half > first half) and the opponent's corner concession is also back-loaded, total match corners rise above the sum of full-match averages — indicating a second-half amplification effect that is only visible when both the half-level split and the cross-team differential are considered jointly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match half-level split of corner kicks for both teams jointly reveals whether corner production is front-loaded (first half) or back-loaded (second half), and this intra-match distribution pattern interacts with each team's full-match corner differential (FOR minus AGAINST) to predict total corner volume in a way that the full-match average alone does not.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires simultaneously using half-level resolution (first vs. second half splits) for both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner rates, then crossing those four half-level values. It is not reducible to a single full-match observable with one coarse band, and the half-level split is a within-match state dimension not covered by the engine's existing two-way splits.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Joint conditioning on: Team A's goals FOR first-half vs. second-half (0.68 vs. 0.83) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half (0.72 vs. 0.65); Team B's goals FOR first-half vs. second-half (0.57 vs. 0.80) and AGAINST first-half vs. second-half (0.62 vs. 0.78). The mechanism tests whether the alignment or misalignment of both teams' half-level goal-rate gradients (i.e., both teams scoring more in the second half) predicts second-half goal volume above what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams exhibit a positive first-to-second-half goal-rate gradient (more goals in second half than first) on both the FOR and AGAINST dimensions, second-half goal volume rises above the competition baseline and above what full-match averages would predict — a within-match state amplification visible only through the joint half-level split across both teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goal-scoring is asymmetrically distributed across halves (0.68 first half vs. 0.83 second half FOR; 0.72 first half vs. 0.65 second half AGAINST), while Team B's goal concession is also asymmetrically distributed (0.62 first half vs. 0.78 second half AGAINST). The joint cross-team half-level goal distribution — where both teams' second-half goal rates diverge from their first-half rates in the same direction — creates a within-match state condition on total goals that full-match averages obscure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneously using half-level resolution for both teams' FOR and AGAINST goal rates (four half-level values), then testing their joint directional alignment. This is a within-match state condition crossed with a cross-team asymmetry — not reducible to a single full-match observable, a single coarse band, or the engine's existing two-way splits.
